quote: So who owns the solar? Who owns the system?
stewart_read: Rep answered with real detail on ownership vs leasing instead of using the escape hatch immediately.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged a brief factual answer necessary to keep an investor-level customer engaged before redirecting — but three separate product questions were each answered rather than bridged.
coaching_implication: Use the universal escape hatch ('that's exactly what our specialist digs into') on the first ownership/product question, not the third.

quote: But what Yes. Companies are you guys talking about?
stewart_read: Rep named the panel manufacturer (Silfab) and microinverter brand (Enphase) unprompted, closer-tier equipment-spec content.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as rapport-building with a technically curious, high-net-worth lead, but it still gives away appointment value the specialist should deliver.
coaching_implication: Redirect equipment-spec questions to the specialist visit rather than reciting manufacturer names.

quote: I got somebody who's who's looking at I got 600,000 to put solar on the resort right now.
stewart_read: Customer disclosed a large-scale, multi-property investment appetite — a strong buying signal.
coaching_implication: Rep should have flagged this explicitly in the specialist notes as a commercial/multi-project opportunity, not just logged 'equipment details.'

quote: I'm not extending this out to the tenants, so I don't know why you'd make that call.
stewart_read: Not the spouse protocol itself, but a related pattern: the ownership-verification hold read as adversarial rather than reassuring to a homeowner defending his sole title.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep's move (checking with manager) is procedurally correct per co_owner verification; the reactive element is the delivery, which triggered defensiveness rather than the substance.
coaching_implication: Lead with reassurance ('just confirming since you own the whole building, this works') before framing it as a possible disqualifier.

quote: Well, you know, that sounds great because I'm interested in the different models.
stewart_read: Customer handed the rep a direct interest-reason (comparing solar models across his properties) and the rep never circled back to tie the appointment to it explicitly.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep did note it for the specialist generally, but never verbally reflected the reason back to the customer as the reason for the appointment.
coaching_implication: Reflect the stated interest back at booking: 'so tomorrow the specialist will walk through model options for your properties' — ties reason to appointment.

quote: the only other thing is find a time, you know, for the specialist to come by.
stewart_read: Booking happened but the button-up skipped the hour-block statement, no-driving/computer instruction, and the 'is that fair' handshake.
coaching_implication: Add the full button-up checklist even when the customer is agreeable — procedural fragility shows up as no-shows later.

quote: am. K. Awesome. So I just heard back. We should be good to go.
stewart_read: Rep's hold-and-return move successfully de-escalated the tenant-billing tension and customer re-engaged cooperatively right after.
coaching_implication: Good recovery — worth reinforcing as a repeatable move for ownership-verification friction.
